title: Your genius father
html_source: This likely refers to Daedalus, who cunningly constructed the labyrinth on Crete in which the minataur was kept, the innovator who, according to Pliny, invented carpentry “and with it the saw, axe, plumb-line, drill, glue, and isinglass.” Pausanius wrote of Daedalus, “All the works of this artist, though somewhat uncouth to look at, nevertheless have a touch of the divine in them.” It most certainly does not refer to Simon Dedalus, whose self-aggrandizing antics Stephen abhors, and yet, perhaps affected by alcohol, exhibits himself in this scene.
